svg.title: EG01 parity panel
svg.desc: The from-scratch Engram and the sw-MLPL engram builtin trained separately at the same table size with the same seed, their results side by side, and the forward and gradient differences measured in each process after copying the trained parameters into the other form.
svg.text: PARITY -- from scratch against the builtin at 256 slots
WHAT: two processes, same seed and data; each ends by loading its trained parameters into the other form.
from scratch: lib/engram.mlpl
ngram_hash + gather_rows + matmul + sigmoid
8708 params, val loss 4.665
builtin: engram / apply_engram
one call, the same five parameters
8708 params, val loss 4.665
measured in the from-scratch process
output difference over 30 held-out windows: 0
table gradient difference: 0
gate-weight gradient difference: 0
measured in the builtin process
output difference over 30 held-out windows: 0
table gradient difference: 0
gate-weight gradient difference: 0
results of the two training runs
scratch: val loss 4.665 prose 0 mlpl 0 nonzero rows 157 gate 0.697
builtin: val loss 4.665 prose 0 mlpl 0 nonzero rows 157 gate 0.697
gate mean per position of 2+3=|5. (percent), scratch then builtin
identical rows mean the two processes trained the same function step for step;
a difference here would be a training-path difference, not a forward-pass one.
WHY: building the mechanism by hand is the lesson; the builtin is the pragmatic form. Both must be the same
function, or the lesson explains something the builtin does not do. HOW: the same seed gives the same initial
projections; the trained table is copied by name (__engram_mem_0) and grad is taken on both forms; tests assert 1e-9.
Limitation: parity is shown on this fixture and size; the hash contract itself is upstream's frozen fixture.
